fields.sample_size: local press review and interviews with women living in the homes closest to the Agua Prieta wastewater plant in Mesa Colorada (Zapopan, Jalisco), home visits and field walks; number of interviewees not extracted
fields.effect_estimate: Since 1989 the Agua Prieta plant treats much of Guadalajara's wastewater while the adjacent segregated Mesa Colorada neighbourhood lacks safe, affordable and sufficient drinking water; the neighbourhood was treated in institutional discourse as a 'sacrifice zone' bearing disproportionate socio-environmental costs of urban water management. Qualitative; no effect estimates.
fields.study_design: qualitative case study (press review, interviews with residents, field observation)
fields.section: Full text: Metodologia (press review, interviews with women, visits); Resultados; Conclusiones
fields.exact_location: Metodologia (press review, interviews with women, visits); Resultados; Conclusiones

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a case study of Mesa Colorada, Zapopan, next to the Agua Prieta wastewater plant, read in full text 2026-10-04 (press review and interviews with women residents). The neighbourhood lacks adequate drinking water while hosting the city's wastewater treatment; framed as a sacrifice zone. Qualitative.
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the method (press review plus interviews with women). Interview count not extracted.
